reason: Throughout this text, when the people voice their opinions and feelings (complaining about hunger in Exodus 16, thirsting in Exodus 17, fear at the sea in Exodus 14), Yahweh's response is consistently compassionate provision—providing manna, quail, and water—not anger. For example, at Exodus 16:8, when the people murmur about food, Moses states that Yahweh 'heard' their complaints and will provide meat and bread. At Exodus 17:6, when the people contend with Moses over water, Yahweh instructs Moses to strike the rock, providing water. There is no instance in this passage where voicing complaints triggers divine anger; rather, complaints are met with provision.
